name: Social Darwinism
summary: Social Darwinism applies ideas of struggle and 'survival of the fittest' to human society, holding that competition rewards the capable and punishes the weak. The label was mostly applied by critics and covers a laissez-faire strand (Spencer, Sumner) that opposes state aid to the poor, a eugenic strand worried about the unfit outbreeding the fit, and racial and militarist strands that justified imperialism and war.
scope: The Anglo-American core of the family: Herbert Spencer's evolutionary social theory and William Graham Sumner's laissez-faire writing, plus the eugenic, racial and militarist applications documented in Wikipedia's article and Bernhardi's Germany and the Next War. Few people called themselves social Darwinists, so the profile is a composite; where strands split (war, empire, state power, equal rights) the answer is 0 or low.

keyFigures.name: Herbert Spencer
keyFigures.role: Coined 'survival of the fittest' and built an evolutionary theory of society.

keyFigures.name: William Graham Sumner
keyFigures.role: American sociologist who defended laissez-faire and large fortunes.

keyFigures.name: Francis Galton
keyFigures.role: Founder of eugenics, who held that mental traits are inherited.

sources.title: Herbert Spencer
sources.author: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
sources.usedFor: Equal freedom, limited state, militant versus industrial society, evolutionary progress, suffrage.

sources.title: What Social Classes Owe to Each Other
sources.author: William Graham Sumner (1883)
sources.usedFor: Laissez-faire, property, large fortunes, equality, the Forgotten Man, opposition to state aid.

sources.title: Germany and the Next War
sources.author: Friedrich von Bernhardi (1911)
sources.usedFor: The militarist strand: war as biological necessity, struggle among nations, rejection of equal rights for weak nations.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Sumner holds it is not the state's function to make men happy and objects to compelled support of others, so state-guaranteed care is rejected.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wages are set by supply and demand, which Sumner treats as a universal law; fixing them by decree is meddling.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Sumner calls the market automatic and self-regulating, and the Spencerian strand wants society ordered by voluntary exchange.

public-ownership.rationale: Industrial society rests on private contract and the state is confined to protecting against force and fraud.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Sumner says the aggregation of large fortunes is not to be regretted and that the Forgotten Man pays for reform schemes.

unions-good.rationale: Inferred from the view that wages follow supply and demand and that no class has a claim on another; unions were not a main subject of the sources.

property-fundamental.rationale: Sumner defends private property as a practical necessity and capital as stored human energy.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Regulation is the kind of social meddling Sumner and Spencer opposed.

cut-welfare.rationale: Poor relief is opposed because it lets the weak survive and breaks the link between conduct and outcome; Sumner warns of the duty to support others.

worker-ownership.rationale: Inferred: ownership follows capital accumulated by individuals; the sources do not discuss co-operatives.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not addressed; the individualist strand would object, the militarist and authoritarian strands would accept.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Anachronistic; Spencerian liberty points to yes, the eugenic and moralising strands to no.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Inferred from the liberal strand's opposition to state restriction and the racial strand's own hierarchy claims.

strong-leader.rationale: Split: Spencer opposed concentrated state power, whereas the militarist strand around Bernhardi stresses strong state leadership.

state-harmful.rationale: The state should be minimal and protect equal freedom; Spencer expected it to recede, but a state with limited functions is retained.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred from the stress on individual liberty and self-reliance.

empower-police-military.rationale: Split between Spencer's opposition to militarism and Bernhardi's call to raise military strength.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; liberty and Victorian morality pull in opposite directions.

decide-locally.rationale: Not addressed beyond the preference for limited central government.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from the hereditarian and consequences-for-conduct emphasis.

traditional-family.rationale: Inferred: eugenic strands valued family reproduction by the fit, and Victorian adherents held conventional norms.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Anachronistic; period adherents held conventional Victorian norms.

abortion-legal.rationale: Anachronistic; eugenic thinkers were divided on birth control and abortion.

more-religion-public.rationale: Spencer rejected theology for science, though some business adherents framed success in religious terms.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The racial strand saw hierarchy as natural, and Sumner says classes owe each other nothing.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from naturalistic, biological explanations of human differences.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The nationalist strand stresses national struggle and character; Spencer-type liberals are less concerned.

gradual-change.rationale: Spencer held that society evolves slowly from simple to complex; inferred as favouring gradual change.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Inferred from the racial and eugenic strands' concern with population quality.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Bernhardi calls arbitration and peace efforts utopian, and the Spencerian strand opposes concentrated authority.

free-trade.rationale: Sumner attacked protective tariffs and monopolies, and the laissez-faire strand backs free exchange.

nation-first.rationale: Bernhardi puts the nation's strength first; the Spencerian strand was anti-imperial but not internationalist.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Inferred: Bernhardi denies weak nations equal claims, and laissez-faire strands oppose foreign adventure.

open-borders.rationale: Inferred from the racial and eugenic strands' views on population quality.

limit-growth.rationale: Inferred from the belief in industrial and economic progress.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from opposition to government intervention in the economy.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Inferred from the belief in evolutionary progress and industrial society.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the pro-industry, pro-progress stance.

revolution-justified.rationale: Society is held to evolve gradually and revolutionary schemes are social meddling.

experts-over-public.rationale: Split: eugenic strands favoured scientific elites; the laissez-faire strand distrusted planners.

central-planning.rationale: Sumner describes the market as automatic and instinctive and plans as ignorant interference.

socialized-markets.rationale: Public or worker ownership is rejected in favour of private property and capital.

land-value-tax.rationale: Split: early Spencer backed common land ownership, later he dropped it; Sumner allowed a land tax only in narrow cases.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Sumner allowed a succession duty narrowly, but the strand favours the fittest families passing on wealth.

basic-income.rationale: Unconditional support for others is the clearest case of what Sumner opposes.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Sumner criticised protective tariffs as favouring monopolies.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Capital allocation belongs to the market, not state officials.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Sumner defends the aggregation of large fortunes as earned and not regrettable.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Capital and wage contracts are central to the free market that Sumner defends.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, and no stated principle settles it either way.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognised bodies setting wages are state direction that contradicts equal freedom and contract.

one-party-rule.rationale: Inferred; Spencer opposed concentrated state power, though the fascist strand embraced it.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Not addressed; adherents were mostly liberal but not necessarily anti-monarchist.

democracy-best.rationale: Spencer concluded that suffrage encouraged over-legislation, and Sumner warned of majorities abusing power.

direct-votes.rationale: Inferred from Sumner's fear of majorities assuming rights and rejecting duties.

workers-councils.rationale: Rejects collective workers' control of production in favour of private ownership.

right-to-secede.rationale: Early Spencer endorsed the right to ignore the state, but he later rejected it.

natural-rulers.rationale: The hierarchy of fitness underlies the idea that some are naturally more capable.

political-violence-never.rationale: Bernhardi treats war as a duty and a biological necessity, so political violence is not always wrong.

war-builds-character.rationale: Split: Bernhardi calls war a biological necessity, while Spencer saw militant society as an earlier stage superseded by industrial peace.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Spencer sought science rather than theology as the basis of society.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Spencer's state exists to protect against force and fraud, so justice and defence stay state functions.

military-superiority.rationale: Bernhardi makes military strength the first duty of the state; Spencerians disagree.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The racial and national strands favour a racially or ethnically defined nation.

class-struggle-history.rationale: They see competition among individuals and peoples as the engine, while Sumner denies that classes owe or oppose each other.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Sumner says equality at the level of the best is plainly impossible and rejects equal outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: The imperialist strand justified expansion over displaced peoples.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The imperialist strand defended colonial rule and Sumner denies obligations between classes.

civilizational-union.rationale: Not addressed; racial strands could favour white or European union, others national struggle.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Sumner treats self-interested competition as the engine of prosperity, but Spencer limited it by ethics.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The Spencerian strand grounds justice in individual liberty limited by others' equal liberty.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Not addressed by the sources, and no stated principle settles it, so adherents are treated as indifferent.

limit-population.rationale: Split: the eugenic strand wanted to restrain the unfit but not generally to limit population.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Spencer saw industrial society as a higher stage of evolution.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Not addressed; progress was seen as gradual and evolutionary.

human-enhancement.rationale: Eugenics favours improving populations, but not freedom of individual choice per se.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from opposition to planners.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Not addressed by the sources, and no stated principle settles it, so adherents are treated as indifferent.

restore-past-order.rationale: Progress through evolution is central, not return to a lost order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Not addressed by the sources, and no stated principle settles it, so adherents are treated as indifferent.

direct-action.rationale: Inferred from the preference for gradual evolution and market order.

means-match-ends.rationale: Not addressed by the sources, and no stated principle settles it, so adherents are treated as indifferent.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Social progress from simple to complex forms is the core theory.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Spencer builds industrial society on the division of labour.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Strength is to be rewarded and weakness not subsidised.

production-for-use.rationale: Production responds to the market and supply and demand.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Sumner calls capital stored energy and profit its earned reward.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Contradicts equal rights and rejects class rule.

collective-farming.rationale: Private property in land is defended in Sumner.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Spencer saw industrial exchange as peaceful; Bernhardi grounds war in biological struggle, not capitalism.

taxation-theft.rationale: Sumner objects to heavy taxation but allows limited taxes.

harm-principle.rationale: Spencer's equal freedom resembles it, but the eugenic and militarist strands accept wider state coercion.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Split between individualist strands and racial or national group struggle strands.

conscription.rationale: Split: Bernhardi's militarism supports it, Spencer opposed.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Early Spencer's right to ignore the state is related but not discussed in these terms.

state-as-business.rationale: Not addressed by the sources, and no stated principle settles it, so adherents are treated as indifferent.

positive-liberty.rationale: Sumner defines liberty as rights and duties in equilibrium and rejects the state's making men happy.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The racial strand ranks races, though not all adherents did.

organic-representation.rationale: Inferred from the individualist and liberal basis.

national-rebirth.rationale: Fascist strands yes, liberal strands no.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Split: Bernhardi says growing nations must take territory, while Spencer opposed imperial expansion.

bound-labor.rationale: Industrial society rests on free contract.

universal-morality.rationale: Spencer sought natural laws of ethics, but other strands were relativist about struggle.

single-common-good.rationale: Individual competition, not a single planned good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not addressed by the sources, and no stated principle settles it, so adherents are treated as indifferent.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not addressed by the sources, and no stated principle settles it, so adherents are treated as indifferent.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not addressed by the sources, and no stated principle settles it, so adherents are treated as indifferent.

school-vouchers.rationale: Spencer opposed state schooling but not specifically public vouchers.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Inferred from opposition to state economic direction.

economic-freedom.rationale: Sumner links liberty to rights, property and competition.

rule-by-example.rationale: Inferred from the law-based equal liberty view.

national-self-determination.rationale: Bernhardi denies weak nations the same right to live as strong ones.

force-without-un.rationale: Bernhardi rejects arbitration and peace institutions.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Spencer put science above theology though he retained the Unknowable.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: They oppose welfare generally, so the restriction question is secondary.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Where relief exists, it should tie to conduct and effort.

class-collaboration.rationale: Sumner denies mutual class duties yet sees contracts as mutually beneficial.

dominated-front.rationale: Inferred from nationalist and imperial strands.

workers-nation.rationale: Nation matters, but this is not a worker-centred view.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Inferred from period norms and biological explanations.

ban-interest.rationale: Capital is defended as stored energy earning return.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Racial strands favoured hierarchy, but liberal strands opposed state laws.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Sumner denies classes dominating each other through the state as the central issue.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Not addressed by the sources, and no stated principle settles it, so adherents are treated as indifferent.

proportional-representation.rationale: Not addressed by the sources, and no stated principle settles it, so adherents are treated as indifferent.

national-mission.rationale: Split between imperialist and anti-imperialist strands.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Sumner critiques reformers and plutocracy; not a general claim.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Not addressed by the sources, and no stated principle settles it, so adherents are treated as indifferent.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: The eugenic strand held that welfare lets the unfit outbreed the capable; Galton did not back restrictive policies.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Spencer limits the state to protecting against force and fraud; Sumner limits it to rights and justice.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The racial strand valued racial purity.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Sumner holds equality of rights; Bernhardi and racial strands deny weak peoples equal claims.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Not addressed by the sources, and no stated principle settles it, so adherents are treated as indifferent.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Early Spencer yes, later less so.

trade-surplus.rationale: Inferred from the free-trade stance of the laissez-faire strand, which treats trade balances as no goal.

population-transfer.rationale: Racial strands might support; liberal strands oppose.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Spencer's equal freedom resembles it; Bernhardi defends war and conquest.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Inferred: the movement presented itself as science discovering natural laws, which implies objective knowledge not shaped by power.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Spencer's evolutionary theory, Sumner's competition and Bernhardi's struggle for existence all treat struggle as what drives social improvement.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Spencerian and Sumnerite strands favour limited government and free association, though militarists differ; inferred.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Spencer's 'equal freedom' is negative liberty, protecting against interference rather than unused power; inferred.

separated-powers.rationale: Spencer and Sumner favoured a limited state and constitutional restraints on legislatures; inferred, strands differ.

vanguard-party.rationale: Social Darwinists did not argue for a leading revolutionary party and generally favoured individual competition; inferred.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Sumner argued that state aid to the poor burdens the 'Forgotten Man' and that society owes the poor no special claim.

missingStatements.text: Competition and struggle, between individuals and between peoples, are the main engine of human progress.
missingStatements.rationale: Spencer's evolutionary theory, Sumner's competition and Bernhardi's struggle for existence all treat struggle as what drives social improvement.

missingStatements.text: Welfare programs create dependency and should be cut.
missingStatements.rationale: Poor relief that lets the weak survive and reproduce is the strand's best-known objection to charity by the state.

notes: The term was mostly applied by critics; Wikipedia notes that some historians think Spencer and Sumner did not strictly apply natural selection to society. Many answers are therefore 0 or low confidence because the strands diverge.
